item.title: Attractive electrons in functional oxide based devices
item.description: Normally, two electrons repel each other because they are both negatively charged. However, colleagues of mine have found that, at the interface between two oxides, electrons can also attract one another. We investigated this effect by exploiting the presence of accidental quantum dots and studying their transport as a function of gate voltage and magnetic field at millikelvin temperatures. I performed modeling to corroborate these exicting experimental results. The full story can be found in this preprint.

item.title: Start Postdoc at DTU!
item.description: I started my postdoc in the group of functional oxdies at the Danish Technical University under supervision of prof. Thomas Sand Jespersen. I will work on two dimensional semiconductor-superconductor membrane devices. This also means that I moved to a new city: Copenhagen! Looking forward to the work and finding my way in this new environment.

item.title: Observing structural crystal distortions in a very thin sandwich of oxides layers
item.description: By stacking thin layers of different materials on top of each other a structural coupling between the layers can be achieved. This coupling can create new and interesting electronic behaviors.

item.title: Superconductivity offers new insights into quantum material
item.description:
Our work on superconductivity in a new quantum material was featured in a blog of the University of Twente written by Kees Wesselink:

For the first time since the discovery of the material MnBi2Te4 (MBT), researchers at the University of Twente have successfully made it behave like a superconductor. This marks an important step in understanding MBT and is significant for future technologies, such as new methods of information processing and quantum computing.
